tools_used: CourtListener MCP: search (dockets, opinions, recap), call_endpoint (docket-entries, clusters, opinions)
helpful: The provisioned application text (134 pages, truncated) carried the whole substantive record: the relief sought, the Ninth Circuit's grounds, and the authorities the applicants lean on.

CourtListener docket-entries on the Ninth Circuit appeal (26-5488) gave the panel, the three amicus filings at that stage, and the appellees' pending extension motion — the amicus-increment and timing forecasts rest on it.

CourtListener opinions endpoint returned the full Mirabelli v. Bonta per curiam, which let me check the posture difference (vacatur of a stay of a merits judgment vs. a first-instance injunction) rather than rely on the applicants' characterization.
The statpack interim table made the strictly-prior pooled baseline computable directly (31/296).
gaps: fedcourts query cannot filter by application kind or applicant class; both --disposition sweeps returned time-extension applications and cert petitions rather than substantive stay/injunction priors, so corpus priors contributed nothing to this cell.

No ladder-conditioned interim rate (grant rate given a requested response) or applicant-class cut (government vs private applicant) in the statpack; the dominant adjustments came from training knowledge of the Court's injunction-pending-appeal practice.
CourtListener holds no text for the Ninth Circuit's published order (plain_text empty), so its reasoning is known only through the applicants' account.
The provisioned application is truncated at 134 pages; the appendix (the lower-court opinions) was not available to read directly.
notes: Retrieval stayed well inside the ~25-call budget (2 corpus queries, 12 MCP calls). Nothing retrieved postdates the snapshot except the Ninth Circuit's 2026-10-05 extension motion, an ordinary forward-mode signal.
